Cause: The vault-agent-init sidecar in the new 3.9.0 pod cannot authenticate to Vault. Its logs show repeated `PUT https://vault.sec.internal:8200/v1/auth/kubernetes-prod/login` returning `Code: 403. permission denied`, so the init container never completes and the pod stays at Init:0/1.

Evidence from the cluster:
- Pod orders-api-5b4d7c8f9-hn6wd (image 3.9.0) is Init:0/1, init container `vault-agent-init` still Running after 41m.
- Pod logs show the Vault login being rejected with 403 (permission denied) and the agent backing off (now at 5m).
- The 3.9.0 pod uses the same ServiceAccount (`orders-api`) and the same Vault annotations (`vault.hashicorp.com/role: orders-api`, `auth-path: auth/kubernetes-prod`, same inject-secret path) as the two healthy 3.8.0 pods, which authenticated fine and are still serving.
- The only change in the release is the application image, which does not affect how Vault validates the login.

A ServiceAccount token presented to an external system is a signed JWT whose claims (issuer, audience, namespace, serviceaccount name, pod reference) are what the receiver validates [cite: concepts/security/service-accounts#authenticating-credentials-0] [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#serviceaccount-token-volume-projection-4]. Nothing on the Kubernetes side of this Pod has changed in a way that would alter those claims (same namespace, same ServiceAccount, same projected-token audience defaults), so the 403 is coming from Vault's own role binding, not from the cluster.

Fix (for the owner to apply): This is not a change the platform team can make — Vault is run by the security team and the 403 is returned by `auth/kubernetes-prod` on their side. Open a request with the security team and give them this evidence. Ask them to check the Vault role `orders-api` on auth path `auth/kubernetes-prod` for:
  1. `bound_service_account_names` still includes `orders-api`.
  2. `bound_service_account_namespaces` still includes `orders`.
  3. The role / Kubernetes auth config was not rotated or re-scoped around 13:00 today (that is when the first 403 appears, matching the deploy time).
  4. Vault's audit log for the login attempts from pod `orders-api-5b4d7c8f9-hn6wd` to see which bound check failed.

Once Vault accepts the login the existing pod will progress past Init on its own (no redeploy needed). The 3.8.0 pods are unaffected and can keep serving in the meantime.
